paper-presentation.description: Paper Presentation is a technical event where participants present innovative ideas, research work, or technical concepts related to Computer Science and related domains. Teams will present their work using presentation slides and explain their idea, methodology, and impact. The event focuses on communication skills, technical knowledge, originality, and the ability to clearly explain complex concepts.

rounds.description: Participants submit their paper abstract before the event. Selected teams will be allowed to present their work during the presentation round.
Each team presents their paper using slides explaining the problem statement, methodology, implementation, and results.
Judges and audience may ask questions about the presented topic to test the participants’ understanding and clarity.

rules_and_regulations.registration_limit: Only the first 30 teams to register will be accepted.
rules_and_regulations.domain: Topics must be related to Computer Science or related domains
rules_and_regulations.originality: Only original work is allowed. Plagiarism is strictly prohibited.
rules_and_regulations.format: Presentation should be prepared using PowerPoint or similar presentation tools.

judging_criteria.description: Understanding of the topic and depth of technical explanation.
Creativity and originality of the idea presented.
Clarity, confidence, and effectiveness in presenting the topic.
Organization of slides, clarity of problem statement, and explanation of solution.
Ability to answer questions confidently and accurately.

code-volt.description: CODE VOLT is a two-member team-based coding and debugging challenge designed to test programming knowledge, logical thinking, code-reading ability, debugging skills, and attention to detail. Unlike conventional coding competitions, participants must understand, reconstruct, debug, and validate existing code while working together under time pressure.

rounds.description: Teams will be presented with 4 programming problems containing incomplete or broken code. Certain lines or critical portions of the logic will be deliberately removed. Participants must understand the existing program, identify the missing logic, reconstruct the required statements, and produce the correct working program.
challenge_points: Understand the given problem and existing code
Test the solution with given inputs

rounds.description: The second round consists of 3 debugging challenges: 2 Jumbled Code challenges and 1 Invalid Test Case challenge. Teams must inspect the given programs, identify hidden problems, restore the correct execution flow, and validate the solution.

challenges.description: Selected lines of a program are deliberately rearranged. Participants must understand the purpose and dependencies of each statement and restore the correct order of execution.
A second program contains incorrectly ordered statements. Teams must analyze variables, conditions, loops, functions, and dependencies to reconstruct the correct program flow.
Participants are given a program and a collection of test cases. They must identify the test case that exposes a flaw, edge case, boundary condition, or incorrect assumption in the implementation.

rules_and_regulations.team_participation: Both participants are expected to actively participate
rules_and_regulations.evaluation: Teams will be evaluated based on accuracy, completion time, and overall performance
rules_and_regulations.fair_play: Any form of cheating, malpractice, or violation of event rules may result in disqualification

prompt-paradox.description: Prompt Paradox is a competitive technical challenge that tests problem-solving, logical thinking, AI literacy, technical reasoning, and decision-making under time pressure.
prompt-paradox.event_duration: Approximately 1 hour 30 minutes to 1 hour 45 minutes

rounds.description: Participants navigate a nonlinear sequence of technical challenges using logic, technical knowledge, and permitted AI assistance. The highest-performing participants or teams will qualify for Round 2.

Qualified participants or teams investigate a technical scenario, analyze evidence, use AI intelligently, verify information, and make a justified technical decision. Three equivalent case scenarios will be used for the qualified participants or teams.

A short Special or Surprise Round may be conducted if required to determine the final rankings. The details will be announced on the spot only if the round is conducted based on the event-day situation.

prompt-paradox.final_ranking: The final ranking will be based on combined performance across the applicable rounds, with round scores converted to an equivalent scale before the final calculation.
prompt-paradox.winners: The Top 3 participants or teams will be declared the winners.

rules_and_regulations.rule_book: Participants must read the Prompt Paradox Participant Rule Book carefully before registering.
rules_and_regulations.registration: Registration indicates that the participant or team has read and agrees to follow the event rules and conditions.

ai-verse.description: AI VERSE is a two-round technical challenge designed for teams of two, combining Generative AI knowledge with practical application development. The event begins with a GenAI Quiz that tests participants on Generative AI concepts, AI tools, application development, programming fundamentals, and emerging AI technologies. Qualified teams will advance to the AI App Forge round, where they will receive a real-world problem statement and use Generative AI to design and develop a functional application within the given time.

rounds.description: Teams will participate in a technical quiz covering Generative AI concepts, Large Language Models, AI tools, prompt-based applications, AI-assisted development, programming fundamentals, and emerging AI technologies.

Qualified teams will receive a real-world problem statement and must design and develop a functional application using Generative AI and AI-assisted development tools. Teams must understand the problem, plan their solution, leverage AI effectively, implement the required features, and submit a working application within the allotted time.

rules_and_regulations.tools: Participants may use Generative AI and AI-assisted development tools available through free tiers or free-access plans.
rules_and_regulations.ai_usage: Only models, tools, APIs, credits, and features accessible through free tiers or free-access plans may be used. Subscription-only models, premium models, paid APIs, purchased credits, and paid-exclusive features are not permitted.
rules_and_regulations.development_tools: Participants may use commonly available programming languages, frameworks, libraries, IDEs, and development tools required to build their application, subject to event guidelines.
rules_and_regulations.submission: The application must be completed and submitted within the allotted time. Late submissions may not be considered.
rules_and_regulations.problem_statement: The problem statement will be provided by the organizers at the beginning of the AI App Forge round.
rules_and_regulations.internet_access: Participants may use internet-accessible resources and permitted AI tools during the development round, subject to the rules announced by the organizers.
rules_and_regulations.originality: The submitted application must be developed by the participating team during the event. Pre-built solutions or previously developed projects may not be submitted.
rules_and_regulations.fair_play: Any misconduct, plagiarism, use of prohibited paid AI services, or violation of event rules may lead to disqualification.

judging_criteria.description: Quality, functionality, reliability, and technical execution of the developed application.
Meaningful, efficient, and appropriate use of Generative AI tools during development.
Understanding of the problem statement and effectiveness, relevance, and practicality of the proposed solution.
Originality, innovative thinking, uniqueness, and creative approach demonstrated in the solution.
Usability, interface quality, user experience, visual design, and clarity of the final application.

reel-and-rhythm.description: Reel & Rhythm is a two-round entertainment challenge that puts participants’ cinema knowledge, musical memory, recognition skills, and response speed to the test. From identifying movies, songs, dialogues, and iconic scenes in REEL RUSH to recognizing songs through beats, instrumentals, humming, and unexpected audio clues in BEAT BREAKER, every challenge demands quick thinking and sharp recognition.

rounds.description: A fast-paced movie and song identification challenge. Participants will be presented with rapid-fire clues and must identify the correct movie, song, character, actor, scene, or other specified answer within the given time.
A music-based identification challenge where familiar songs are presented through unconventional musical clues.

clue_types.description: Identify the song from its beat or rhythmic pattern.
Identify the song from a vocal-free instrumental section.
Identify the song from its melody being hummed.
Identify the original song from creatively altered audio such as reversed, slowed, shortened, or modified clips.

buzzer_system.description: A buzzer-based answering system will determine which team gets the first opportunity to answer.
rules: Each team may use one smartphone to access the digital buzzer.
The team that activates the buzzer first will be given the opportunity to answer.
In case of network or technical failure, an assigned physical flag system will be used.
Teams must raise their flag clearly to indicate that they wish to answer.
If multiple teams buzz or raise their flags simultaneously, the organizers will determine the response order.
Only the team recognized by the organizers may provide the answer.
The organizers’ decision regarding buzzer order will be final.

reel-and-rhythm.qualification: Based on Round 1 scores, the organizers will determine which participants or teams advance to Beat Breaker.
reel-and-rhythm.tie_breaker: If two or more teams finish with the same score, an additional tie-breaker challenge may be conducted.
rules_and_regulations: Each participant may register for only one team.
Team members must be finalized before the event begins.
Answers must be given within the specified time limit.
Answers submitted after the time limit may not be accepted.
Participants may discuss answers only within their registered team.
Mobile phones may be used only for the designated buzzer system during active gameplay.
Internet searches, external assistance, smartwatches, earphones, or other unauthorized resources are not permitted during the challenges.
Participants must not record or distribute questions, clues, or audio used during the event.
Any form of cheating, unauthorized assistance, or deliberate disruption may result in disqualification.
Participants must follow the instructions of the event coordinators throughout the competition.
The organizers may modify the number of questions, time limits, or round structure if required for the smooth conduct of the event.
The organizers’ decision regarding answers, buzzer order, scoring, qualification, tie-breakers, and rule interpretation will be final.

wit-and-will.description: WIT & WILL is a thrilling two-round team challenge that combines puzzles, observation, strategy, negotiation, teamwork, and quick decision-making. Teams compete through a series of unexpected challenges designed to test both their intelligence and determination.

rounds.description: Teams solve a series of riddles, puzzles, decoding challenges, observation tasks, hidden connections, and time-based challenges. Each correct solution earns points.

challenges.description: A coded message is given using numbers or symbols. Teams must decode it within 2 minutes.
Two similar images are shown for 30 seconds. Teams must identify as many differences as possible.
Teams are given 3–4 clues and must find the common connection.
Teams must identify the missing number or letter in a sequence.
Teams solve tricky riddles within a limited time.
challenges.example: I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. I have no body, but I come alive with wind.

challenges.description: A combination of emojis or images represents a word, movie, phrase, or concept. Teams must identify the answer.

rounds.description: Teams take part in interactive physical and strategic challenges that test negotiation, coordination, decision-making, risk-taking, teamwork, adaptability, and determination.

wit-and-will.winner: The team with the highest combined score from both rounds wins.

player-auction.description: Details for the Player Auction event will be announced soon.
